subject: Clarifying commit tiers, quarterly true-up & make-goods for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna.liu@nimbushealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API commit question — how does true-up / make-good work?

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks very promising for our care-coordination workflows. Before we take a formal pricing review with procurement, I need to clarify a few mechanics around the commit tier you outlined:

- If we sign a usage-based commit (e.g., $600k/year equivalent), how does Redwood handle a shortfall at quarter or year-end? Is there a true-up or make-good credit?
- Can committed discounts be applied per-token across all models or only to specific tiers/models?
- What happens with overage months — are they billed at on-demand rates, or can those tokens be counted toward the next quarter?

Our CFO (cc'd) is sensitive to large upfront commitments and wants to understand downside protection. Can you send a short summary of the true-up cadence and an example calculation?

Cheers,
Anna Li
Head of ML Platform
Nimbus Health

Attachments: none
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit question — how does true-up / make-good work?

Hi Anna / Tom,

Great questions — below is a concise breakdown of our standard proposal and a couple of optional protections we can add for Nimbus. I’ll also attach a one-page worked example and a draft term sheet.

1) Commit coverage and discounts
- Commit is expressed as an annual token commitment and maps to a tiered volume discount (applies across all hosted API calls unless you designate a carve-out for a private model). Example tiers we typically propose: 250k USD/year (15% off), 600k USD/year (28% off), 1.2M USD/year (35% off). These are illustrative — we can tune to your target ARR.

2) Quarterly true-up mechanics (default)
- We reconcile committed tokens vs actual usage at the end of each quarter.
- If actual usage >= pro-rated commit for the quarter, you keep the discount; no action required.
- If actual usage < pro-rated commit, we offer a make-good credit applied to the next invoice. For Nimbus, proposed default: make-good equals 100% of the shortfall for the first contract year (i.e., we credit the difference at the committed discount level). After year one, make-goods cap at 50% of the quarterly shortfall.

3) Overage handling
- Overage tokens beyond the committed quantity in a quarter are billed at on-demand list rates.
- We can optionally allow a one-quarter carryover of unused committed tokens to absorb a later spike (up to 25% of the quarterly commitment), subject to availability.

4) Examples (attached)
- I attached pricing_calc_nimbus.xlsx — two scenarios: mild under-utilization (Q1 short by 18%) and growth burst (Q3 over by 35%). The workbook shows the invoice line-level impacts.

5) Next steps
- If that aligns, I’ll send a term sheet (Redwood_Commit_Terms_v3.pdf) with the specific numbers we discussed and a DocuSign link for signature. Marissa (cc) will help finalize contract language for the make-good and rollback clauses.

Open to a short call tomorrow to walk the example.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Marissa / Vivek,

Need quick alignment for Nimbus Health. They are most comfortable with a commit ~600k USD/year (annualized) but want downside protection if usage lags in the first year. My proposal in the reply: quarterly true-up, 100% make-good of shortfall in year 1 (credit applied next invoice), then 50% cap thereafter. Also offering optional 1-quarter carryover up to 25% of quarterly commit to help seasonal spikes.

Questions:
- Approve 100% make-good for the first year? Hit to revenue will show as credit but we want to avoid long-term exposure.
- Can Legal sign off on a 25% one-quarter carryover?

Relevance: deal pipeline expects decision by 5/26. I attached the draft terms and the Excel calc.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Vanessa —

Thanks for the summary. I’m okay with the suggested structure with a couple of guardrails:

- Approve 100% make-good for the first contract year only (limited-term concession to win the proof-of-value).
- After year 1, make-goods capped at 50% of quarterly shortfall and cannot be accumulated beyond 2 quarters.
- Carryover: allow 1-quarter carryover up to 25% of quarterly commit, but document that carryover is one-time and contingent on capacity/availability. We should also add a clause that reserves Redwood the right to deny carryover if the committed pool is capacity-constrained.
- Legal to add language limiting aggregate credits to protect revenue recognition (we'll record as contra-revenue / credit memos).

If that sounds good, Vanessa — offer this formally to Nimbus. We can flex the discount tier slightly if they sign an early commitment.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Hi Anna / Tom — following up with the formalized guidance after internal approval. Summary of the offer we can put in the term sheet: 

1) Commit & discount: 600k USD/year commit — 28% effective discount across hosted API (applies to per-token billing for all models on hosted plane unless you request a carve-out).

2) True-up cadence: quarterly reconciliation.

3) Make-good (shortfall protection):
- Year 1: Redwood will credit 100% of the quarterly shortfall (i.e., the difference between the pro-rated committed spend and actual billed spend) as an account credit applied to the following invoice.
- Year 2+: make-goods capped at 50% of a quarterly shortfall and cannot be accumulated beyond two consecutive quarters.

4) Carryover & overage:
- Optional: one-quarter carryover of unused committed tokens up to 25% of a quarterly commitment (subject to capacity — Redwood reserves right to deny if capacity constrained).
- Overage tokens beyond the combined committed + carryover volume billed at standard on-demand rates.

5) Operational notes:
- Credits are applied as invoice line-item credits (not cash refunds) and will be reflected in monthly billing.
- We’ll include a worked example in the term sheet and the attached pricing_calc_nimbus.xlsx.

If Nimbus agrees to these protections, I’ll send Redwood_Commit_Terms_v3.pdf with the specific numbers and DocuSign link. Would you like the DocuSign to route for signature to Tom first, or Anna?

Thanks — happy to set a 20-minute call to walk through the workbook.
